summary: An excerpt from a fiction work (Book 10, part 38) in which a VC visits a craftsperson's studio in Pico Rivera and examines her sculptures made from discarded electronics such as old phones, game consoles and inner-tube strips. The VC is moved by the objects' emotional weight and nostalgia, and the artist explains she sells only through in-person commissions and refuses online sales. The scene closes with the two debating whether her craft can scale, which she disputes by breaking the business into four elements that each scale.
one_line: A venture capitalist visits an artist in Pico Rivera who makes sculptures from discarded electronics and debates whether her business can scale.
key_facts: The VC visits a studio in Pico Rivera where the artist makes sculptures from discarded electronics.
One sculpture has eyes bearing HP and Playstation logos and lips made from inner-tube strips bearing small logomarks.
The artist says a device she made will work like an old-time phone and can do a lookup from old-style exchange numbers to identity registers to attempt a voice-call.
The artist says most buyers want the objects for their object-ness and the emotion they carry rather than the phone function.
The VC says the scuffs and scratches on the pieces are like stories, each a memento mori for a long-dead instant in a stranger's life.
One sculpture is made from several generations of iPhones, with screens carved into abstract shapes and painted with networked OLEDs stitched into a single display.
The artist tosses a sculpture high and lets it land on the floor, saying it cannot break because it is made of garbage.
The VC says he remembers wanting these objects as a child, when each seemed impossibly wonderful and out of reach.
The artist says she mostly takes commissions, only from people who visit in person, and will not sell online.
The artist says getting off email was the best gift she ever gave herself.
The artist says she is easy to reach and that visitors can park at her studio if they are that kind of pervert.
The VC says she cannot scale the business even with all the money in the world, which the artist disputes.
The artist says her business decomposes into four elements: materials acquisition, design, fabrication and retail, and that all of them scale like crazy.
